tasks.short: Use protective equipment against infectious diseases

steps.what: Select, fit and use masks, gloves and safety glasses during patient care

tasks.design: Retain physical protective-equipment selection and use. Existing infection-control guidance in {DOCS} supports practice; software does not put on, change or safely remove protective barriers.
tasks.previous_blocker: Protection requires physical action throughout care.
tasks.enabler_now: No supported digital change removes the action.
tasks.still_hard: Consistent fit and replacement during clinical work.
tasks.human_edge: The dentist recognises contamination and follows safe handling practices.
tasks.altitude: No change in protection work or responsibility.

evidence.claim: Protective-equipment use remains physical work in this scenario.

assumptions: Boundary is dentist protective-equipment use, excluding procurement and separate infection-control documentation.
Dentist observes the care activity and selects equipment within s1's100 hours; no structured contamination or readiness flag is assumed.
No process or tool is added, so incremental upkeep is zero.
research_questions: Which protective-equipment actions are physical and already supported by current guidance?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 and zero upkeep; no physical protection time is removed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Formulate treatment plans for teeth and mouth tissue

steps.what: Assess the patient's teeth, mouth tissue, history and treatment preferences
Formulate and discuss the plan of treatment and resolve clinical tradeoffs

tasks.design: Retain assessment and treatment-plan formulation with the dentist, supported by {OTHER}, the existing dental clinical record. The digest's note-drafting capabilities do not establish automated dental treatment selection.
tasks.previous_blocker: Treatment depends on clinical findings and individual preferences.
tasks.enabler_now: No supported change removes the clinical judgement in this boundary.
tasks.still_hard: Balancing prognosis, invasiveness, affordability and patient goals.
tasks.human_edge: The dentist integrates findings and discusses appropriate options.
tasks.altitude: No change in planning time or clinical decision rights.

evidence.claim: Individual dental treatment planning remains clinical judgement in this scenario.

assumptions: Boundary includes assessment and plan discussion, excluding treatment delivery and separately owned chart documentation.
Dentist establishes findings and preferences in s1's55 hours. No structured diagnosis or treatment-choice input is assumed to exist without that assessment.
Existing records remain baseline tools; no new upkeep is introduced, justifying zero incremental work.
unknowns: Typical case complexity and planning process
research_questions: Is repeated documentation separate from actual treatment judgement?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 and zero upkeep; assessment and treatment decisions are retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Design and fit appliances or issue fabrication instructions

steps.what: Assess appliance needs and determine the patient-specific design and specifications
Write, verify and issue fabrication instructions for dental technicians
Make or fit the prosthodontic appliance and check function and comfort

tasks.design: Use a native fabrication form in {OTHER}, the dental clinical system, to reuse dentist-selected appliance specifications. The dentist checks every instruction before issue and retains all design, making, fitting and functional checks.
tasks.previous_blocker: Selected design details can be copied repeatedly into fabrication instructions.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable structured forms can place checked specifications without generating a clinical design.
tasks.still_hard: Patient-specific fit and functional compromises need clinical judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The dentist chooses the design and verifies its performance in the mouth.
tasks.altitude: Slightly less instruction entry; design and fitting responsibility remain unchanged.

evidence.claim: Native fabrication forms can reduce repeated entry of dentist-selected specifications; no measured dental result is supplied.

assumptions: Boundary is dentist design, instructions and hands-on appliance work. Shares represent a workload mix; laboratory manufacturing labour is excluded and not treated as saving.

Dentist produces patient and case identity, appliance type, tooth or site designation, selected material and case-specific instructions in s1's30 hours. Missing or unusual specifications are entered manually and checked in s2's9 remaining hours. No structured design is supplied for free by an algorithm.
Test native forms first. Cases requiring specialist free-text instructions remain manual; no model or automatic design decision is needed.
unknowns: Existing instruction forms and repeated entry share
Mix of in-house and laboratory cases
research_questions: Does field reuse reduce instruction time after a complete clinical check?

incremental.description: Maintain fabrication form fields and handle exceptions

approvals.approved_version: Exact final fabrication instructions, patient case identity and destination technician; any change voids approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R94, gross6 minus2 upkeep net4. Low assumes only2 hours repeat entry removed;85 hours design and hands-on work remain unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Advise patients on prevention, dental problems and oral health services

steps.what: Explore the patient's oral health understanding, concerns and care habits
Advise and instruct patients about prevention, dental problems and available care services

tasks.design: Keep individual advice, demonstration and understanding checks human. Existing patient material in {DOCS} can support the conversation without replacing it or creating an assumed writing workload.
tasks.previous_blocker: Advice must fit individual understanding and dental needs.
tasks.enabler_now: No supported change removes the patient conversation.
tasks.still_hard: Fear, misconceptions and practical barriers to prevention.
tasks.human_edge: The dentist adapts advice and checks what the patient can apply.
tasks.altitude: No change in advice time or clinical responsibility.

evidence.claim: Patient-specific advice and understanding checks remain human work in this scenario.

assumptions: Boundary is live advice, excluding treatment planning and separate patient-material drafting.
Dentist elicits concerns and habits in s1's30 hours; no structured adherence or readiness flag is assumed.
Existing guidance remains baseline material. No new tool or upkeep is introduced, justifying zero incremental work.
research_questions: Which preventive advice needs demonstration and individual follow-up?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 and zero upkeep; no patient communication time is removed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: These clinical and physical tasks mostly retain their time; only repeated fabrication-instruction entry has a modest opportunity.
reach: Clarify fabrication specifications with dental technicians
Develop preventive explanations with dental hygienists
role.ambitious_version: A dentist who simplifies repeated form entry while retaining clinical judgement, protective practices and patient contact.
